title: add compact retrospective-snippet export and anonymized oncall notes CLI
author: Ava Morales
release_notes: Adds an opt-in CLI and internal API to export compact, anonymized ‘retrospective snippets’ for each oncall shift. Useful for quick postmortems, handoffs, and retrospective-summaries. Backwards compatible behind feature flag 'retrospective_snippets_v1'.
description:
Motivation: Oncall handoffs and postmortems often need a compact, privacy-safe snapshot of what happened during a shift: key incidents, actions taken, outstanding items, and suggested follow-ups. Existing incident-bot artifacts are rich but large and require manual sanitization for broader sharing. This PR adds a new export path and lightweight CLI that produces anonymized, context-aware 'retrospective snippets' suitable for internal retros, incident timelines, or automated follow-up generators.

What this change does: Implements a compact export pipeline and CLI 'ibctl retrospective export' that: (1) aggregates incident references, alert summaries, and responder notes for a single shift window; (2) applies deterministic de-identification (email/domain redaction, tokenized user handles, IP truncation) and a configurable PII-safe whitelist; (3) ranks and trims entries by relevance using a simple TF-IDF score over a short context window so the export remains < 200KB by default; (4) emits exports as newline-delimited JSON (jsonl) and an optional markdown digest; (5) supports gzip compression and an S3-compatible upload target. The feature is gated behind the feature flag 'retrospective_snippets_v1' and respects RBAC (only users with 'oncall:export' scope can run it).

Design notes: Export format is intentionally minimal: each snippet entry contains shift_id, incident_refs, timestamp, snippet_text (redacted), tags, and a list of 'followups' synthesized from action items. We maintain a compact provenance header with request_id, tool_version, and anonymization rules applied. Redaction is tuned to err on the side of privacy: unrecognized tokens are replaced with stable pseudonyms (user_####) instead of heuristically trying to guess names.

CLI examples:
- Export a single shift to local file: ibctl retrospective export --shift 2026-02-08T18:00Z --out ./snippets.jsonl
- Upload and compress: ibctl retrospective export --shift 2026-02-08T18:00Z --out s3://company-oncall/snippets/shift-20260208.jsonl.gz --compress gzip --upload
- Dry run (no upload, show top 5 snippets): ibctl retrospective export --shift 2026-02-08T18:00Z --dry-run --limit 5

Privacy & safety: The export pipeline contains a deterministic redaction step plus a layered PII-checker that flags high-confidence PII for manual review instead of auto-including it. There's an admin toggle to include verbatim (unredacted) output for compliance/audit customers but that path requires additional KMS-backed approval. The default behavior for hosted runs is strict redaction.

Implementation summary: Changes touch the export pipeline, a new 'retrospect' subcommand, sanitization library additions, unit + e2e tests, and a short doc in the oncall guide. Key files added/modified are listed below. The core anonymizer lives in pkg/anonymize with a deterministic pseudonymizer and a rule-set that maps to config/retrospective.yml. We added a lightweight ranker in pkg/snippet/ranker.go (TF-IDF over short fields) to keep exported size predictable.
commits_summary:
1) initial scaffold for retrospective export and CLI (cmd/retrospect, pkg/snippet)
2) add anonymizer and deterministic pseudonymizer (pkg/anonymize)
3) add TF-IDF ranker and size trimming, tests and fixtures
4) docs and feature flag wiring
5) CI tweaks for S3 retry and test stability
review_conversation:
Noah Chen: Overall nice and focused; two asks: make the default limit 100 snippets (instead of 200) and add a unit test for IP redaction edge-case.
Ava Morales: Made the default 100 and added the test for 10.0.0.0/8 redaction edge-case; pushed fix.
Priya Singh: Security thumbs-up on redaction approach; asked for explicit docs on pseudonymization determinism.
Ava Morales: Added a short section in docs/retrospective-threatmodel.md describing the stable salt per-org and rotation policy.
Jordan Kim: Found a race in test harness on CI; requested adding retry-window.
Ava Morales: Added retry and re-ran CI — all green.
Approvals: Noah Chen approved, Priya Singh approved, Jordan Kim approved. Merge method: squash and merge.

notes: This PR is intentionally conservative about what is redacted. If teams need richer exports, follow-up work will add per-org opt-in policies and an auditable approval flow.
manual_steps:
1. Ensure feature flag retrospective_snippets_v1 is off in production config.
2. Deploy binary with new CLI but keep flag off.
3. For internal testing, enable flag for a single org and run: ibctl retrospective export --shift <shift-id> --out ./test.jsonl
4. Inspect attached docs/docs/oncall/retrospective-snippets.md for guidance.
5. If uploading to S3, ensure oncall-export service account has s3:PutObject limited to prefix.
